messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: svc/redwood-embed returned 5xx spike (500->502) in us-east-1 canary at 2412345600. Error rate > 8% over 2m. Tags: ci:canary, image:registry.redwood.dev/redwood/embed:latest

oncall-bot: Pager triggered for channel: #eng-oncall — Severity: P2. Paging maya (primary oncall).

maya: seeing it. Checking canary logs + recent deploys. Anyone touching embed pipeline in last hour?

liam: I triggered a canary rollout 17m ago for the embed image. CI reported green but I saw some flaky cache hits.

maya: ok liam — what's the image tag/digest used in the canary?

liam: image=registry.redwood.dev/redwood/embed:20260314-6789 (expected digest: sha256:abc123...)

maya: pulling the canary image locally to inspect layers. Running: 
```
docker pull registry.redwood.dev/redwood/embed:20260314-6789
skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.dev/redwood/embed:20260314-6789 --raw | jq -r '.config.digest'
```

maya: skopeo shows digest sha256:def999... which does NOT match CI's recorded digest (sha256:abc123...). that's suspicious.

kai: ugh, we saw a mutable tag race in the last pipeline stage on a flimsy registry mirror earlier. Possibly retagged or cache-poisoned layer pushed over the same tag.

henry: logs from pods show runtime error when loading custom tokenizer weights: "Invalid layer format at offset 0x4f2b" — looks like a mismatched layer blob.

maya: customer impact: embeddings endpoint 502 for ~10% of traffic routed to the canary. Most traffic on stable is fine but a few customers on canary experienced failures. Support, please triage cs tickets. @support-bot flag impacted orgs in the last 30m.

support-bot: Notified customers with origins using canary: org-redwood-test, partner-x, sandbox-42. Templated note queued for CS to send.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) Kill the canary weight / flip feature flag to 0 2) Pause CI pipeline and block new tags 3) Investigate registry for retag/mutable-notary issues 4) Rebuild artifact with immutable manifest and release properly signed 5) Postmortem and CI guardrail to verify digest before rollout

kai: opening kill-switch now. Running `redwoodctl rollout set-weight svc/redwood-embed canary 0 --reason "canary artifact mismatch"`

deploy-bot: Rollout update: canary weight set to 0 for svc/redwood-embed by kai. Traffic switched to stable at 2412345722.

maya: good. watch error rate drop.

henry: error rate dropped to normal after 18s. 502 -> 0.8%. canary pods terminated.

liam: paused CI: disabled trigger for embed pipeline (ci/pipelines/embed). Will block merges to main until we confirm artifact integrity.

maya: can we confirm whether this is retag in registry or CI wrote wrong manifest? Steps: list manifests for that tag, check object store timestamps, and check registry audit.

kai: registry audit shows a push at 2412345100 of digest sha256:abc123... then another push at 2412345400 of digest sha256:def999... under same tag. Source IPs: builder-03 (CI) pushed first, then mirrored from mirror-07. Mirror pushed later with overwrite. Looks like mirror allowed mutable tags and rewrote the tag to a different digest.

liam: mirror-07 is part of our edge registry caching infra — we recently enabled auto-retag for hot layers to reduce pulls. That was naive.

maya: immediate next steps: 1) disable mirror auto-retagging 2) revert mirror tag policy to read-through-only 3) retag stable images to immutable digest-based tags and push 4) audit CI to write signed manifests (cosign) and require digest acceptance during rollout

henry: for immediate customer-facing mitigation I've pushed a temporary policy to route all canary-eligible customers off canary via traffic-router. Command: `trafficctl set-route embed canary-exclude org-redwood-test,partner-x,sandbox-42`

support-bot: Noted. CS will send follow-up. Recommended message: "We briefly routed you off an experimental canary yesterday after we detected an integrity mismatch in the canary artifact. No production data was lost. We're rebuilding the canary with immutable images and will follow up with more details."

liam: started a clean rebuild with cache disabled: `CI_DISABLE_CACHE=1 ./ci/build-embed.sh && ./ci/publish --tag 20260314-6789-immutable --cosign` Will force a new digest and sign it.

kai: I've also added a temporary CI gate step to verify `skopeo inspect` digest after push and compare to recorded digest before returning success. If mismatch, fail the build and alert eng-infra.

maya: good. Add a periodic job to verify tags on edge mirrors don't diverge from upstream. Also ensure registry returns 409 on attempts to overwrite immutable tags.

henry: pushing quick fix to mirror config now. patch: 
```
# mirror-07 config snippet
allow_overwrite: false
enforce_immutable_tags: true
```

henry: mirror-07 patched and restarted. audit job queued to scan tags changed in last 24h.

liam: rebuild completed and cosigned. New tag: 20260314-6789-immutable digest=sha256:fedcba9876543210. Pushing to registry primary now.

deploy-bot: CI publish success for registry.redwood.dev/redwood/embed:20260314-6789-immutable (signed).

maya: plan to do a cautious canary re-deploy at 1% weight, monitor for 5m. Use traffic shaping to isolate known orgs from the experiment.

kai: starting canary: `redwoodctl rollout set-weight svc/redwood-embed canary 1 --image 20260314-6789-immutable`

henry: canary pods are up and pulling signed image; digest matches cosign. healthchecks green.

maya: monitoring: latency, 5xx, tokenizer load errors. If anything >1% error for 2m revert immediately.

sophia: incoming night oncall handoff in 20m. maya, anything you want to call out for next shift?

maya: handoff notes:
- Root cause: mirror allowed overwriting a hot tag which caused a divergent digest (cache/retag race).
- Impact: ~10% of canary traffic saw 5xx for embeddings; small set of customers on canary affected; no stable traffic affected.
- Mitigation done: canary weight forced to 0; mirror overwrite disabled; CI gate added to verify digest and cosign; rebuild with immutable tag and cosign; canary re-deploy at 1% with isolation.
- Follow-ups: create postmortem, add registry immutable enforcement, add monitoring for tag-digest divergence, add canary-aware customer routing to avoid exposing orgs by default.

sophia: thanks — I'll take the rest. I'll watch the canary and pause if any anomaly. Will update the incident channel and schedule a postmortem with eng-infra + ci owners tomorrow.

maya: thanks all. good coordination. :thumbsup:

sophia: I'm on. taking the incident to stabilization -> monitoring. Will ping here on any regression.

deploy-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity lowered to P3 at 2412345890.

sophia: handing off to night oncall doc: https://confluence.redwood.dev/oncall/handoffs/2412345678. Leave any notes here and I'll pick up.

maya: added initial timeline + evidence to the confluence page.

liam: filing a CI ticket to add explicit digest recording + cosign requirement: CI-ISSUE-3245.

kai: filing registry hardening ticket: REG-712.

henry: scheduling a mirror-scan job to run hourly for 24h.

sophia: copy. will run a quick sweep at 2300 local and report.

support-bot: CS notifications sent to affected orgs. Ticket numbers: CS-9981, CS-9982.

maya: closing notes: if you see any residual 502s, escalate immediately. otherwise we'll convert this to a postmortem and attach artifacts.

sophia: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything pops.
